title: CIF playoffs first round, quarterfinals San Joaquin County boys, girls water polo scores - NewsBreak
text:
By Dylan Ackermann ,
9 hours ago Ladies and gentlemen, the 2025 CIF Sac-Joaquin Section boys and girls water polo playoffs are here.
Seven girls’ and seven boy's teams will represent San Joaquin County in this year’s high school tournament.
For the girls, first-round play began Tuesday, Nov. 4, with quarterfinals set for Thursday, Nov. 6. The boys, meanwhile, dive into first-round action Wednesday, Nov. 5, followed by quarterfinals on Friday, Nov. 7.
On the girls’ side, St. Mary’s enters the postseason as the county’s top-ranked team and a top-25 program in the state. The Rams, seeded No. 2 in Division II, rolled to the Tri-City Athletic League title and stacked up 18 wins along the way. Their nine losses? All against California powerhouses — four to top-six teams (one faced twice), two to top-15 programs, and three more ranked inside the top 30.
Not far behind is Lodi, the TCAL runner-up. The Flames, seeded No. 6 in Division II, are better than their record suggests. Like St. Mary’s, they endured a grueling non-league schedule and, if not for the Rams, likely would’ve coasted to a league title of their own.
It’s the TCAL’s depth, however, that makes their league runs even more impressive — all but two teams qualified for the Division II postseason. No. 8 Tracy dropped just four games, No. 10 Bear Creek won 20, and No. 13 Kimball beat every county team it faced outside the league. They, too, deserve plenty of respect.
Outside the TCAL, only two girls teams reached the postseason — No. 9 Sierra in Division II and No. 12 Oakdale in Division III. Sierra dominated the Valley Oak League, going a perfect 8-0, with no other team finishing within four wins. Oakdale, meanwhile, placed fourth.
On the boys’ side, all signs point to Lodi. The Flames, No. 2 in Division II, rolled to the TCAL crown and looked every bit the part. They beat No. 11 St. Mary’s three times, topped No. 3 Ripon by five goals and crushed No. 13 Tracy by 13 and 15. Not to discredit anyone else — it just shows how consistent and commanding Lodi has been.
Ripon, though, might say one game doesn’t tell the whole story. The Indians land right behind at No. 3 in Division II after tearing through the Valley Oak League. Each of their nine losses came against teams ranked inside or close to California’s top 100 — a mark of how battle-tested this group really is.
One goal. Two goals. One goal in double overtime. That’s how tight No. 11 St. Mary’s battles with Lodi were — and maybe the difference between No. 2 and No. 11. It's that close.
No. 13 Tracy and No. 15 Sierra might not have topped the standings, but playing in two of the county’s toughest Division II leagues could pay off when it matters most. Time will tell.
Oakdale, No. 4 in Division III, took second in the Valley Oak League, and Tokay, No. 16 in Division I, finished fourth in the Delta League.
That’s the setup. Now, let’s get to what everyone’s here for — the results.
Here's the all-in-one resource for updates, results and schedules across the San Joaquin County area this week.
All games will be played at the home pool unless otherwise noted.
